Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Financial Group Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Apex Financial Group's results for the Q2 2024. With me this morning are David Marshall, Chief Executive Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Financial Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to David Marshall.

David Marshall:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Financial Group delivered solid performance in the Q2, demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model and our commitment to serving our customers.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Enhancing customer experience
2. Driving operational efficiency
3. Investing in strategic growth initiatives
4. Maintaining strong capital levels.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our overall company performance, efficiency ratio progress, reserve dynamics, and outlook for loan growth and credit quality.

Starting with overall performance, this marked our strongest quarter in over a decade, with record profitability against a resilient economic backdrop. We posted adjusted net revenues of $15.8 billion, reflecting a 14% year-over-year increase and 3% quarter-over-quarter growth, surpassing consensus estimates of $15.4 billion. Adjusted net income reached $4.3 billion, up 18% from last year, yielding diluted EPS of $1.92—beating expectations by $0.12 and extending our streak of 11 consecutive quarters of double-digit earnings growth.

On the interest income front, net interest margin widened to 3.72%, gaining 22 basis points sequentially and 45 basis points year-over-year. This stemmed from our deposit beta of only 32%—below industry norms—and targeted repricing in our $450 billion commercial loan portfolio, where yields climbed to 5.8% from 5.2% a year earlier. Total loans expanded 9% year-over-year to $1.2 trillion, led by 12% growth in high-yield commercial and industrial lending, plus gains in renewables and middle-market tech sectors that now comprise 15% of the book. Consumer loans, encompassing autos and credit cards, rose 7%, bolstered by our co-branded Visa Infinite rewards program.

Non-interest revenue accelerated 22% year-over-year to $5.1 billion, accounting for 32% of total revenues and underscoring our fee diversification efforts. Wealth and asset management fees soared 25% to $1.8 billion, fueled by $120 billion in net new advisory assets, pushing AUM to $2.4 trillion. Our Apex Wealth AI robo-advisor platform added 450,000 digital clients, using machine learning akin to BlackRock's Aladdin for tailored ESG portfolios. Investment banking fees climbed 30% to $1.2 billion, thanks to $45 billion in M&A advisory, including a $12 billion private equity carve-out of a regional rail operator, alongside 18 IPOs. Trading in our corporate and investment banking unit stayed firm at $900 million, with fixed income up 15% amid Fed-driven volatility.

Credit metrics stayed excellent, validating our vintage underwriting approach. Provisions for credit losses were $450 million, down 10% quarter-over-quarter, while net charge-offs held at 45 basis points—flat year-over-year and under peers like JPMorgan at 52 basis points. Consumer credit card delinquencies edged to 1.2% seasonally, but office CRE, limited to 2% of loans, avoided downgrades, supported by $500 million in stress-tested restructurings. Our CECL reserve is 1.15% of loans, prudently positioned versus Bank of America's 1.25%.

By region, our U.S. operations—60% of earnings—drove 16% profit growth, with $35 billion in deposit inflows to high-yield savings at 4.25% APY, outperforming Wells Fargo's beta dynamics. Europe grew 10% despite ECB cuts, capturing 8% cross-border payments share via SEPA Instant with 150 million transactions from our Dublin hub. Asia-Pacific shone with 25% growth from 12% loan expansion in Singapore and India, powered by our Grab partnership for embedded finance and BNPL, generating $800 million in fees. Emerging markets NPLs stayed below 1%, aided by our AI early warning system outperforming traditional models by 20%.

On strategy, our AWS core banking modernization Phase 2 migrated 70% of workloads, slashing mainframe costs 28% like U.S. Bancorp's post-integration. Gen-AI fraud detection with Palantir cut false positives 40% and saved $150 million. CET1 rose to 12.8%, up 40 basis points, enabling $2.5 billion buybacks and a 12% dividend increase to $0.48 per share. ROTCE reached 17.2%, leading large-cap peers, setting up tuck-in M&A like last year's $1.2 billion wealth manager deal.

I will now turn the call over to Robert Kline to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, David, and good morning. Apex Financial Group reported net income of $4.3 billion for the Q2, or $1.92 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 14% driven by higher interest rates and loan growth. Non-interest income surged 22% on robust fee momentum.

Next, on our efficiency ratio—a core measure of adjusted non-interest expense over total revenue, where lower is better— we made solid strides. For full-year 2023, it improved to 56.2%, a 210 basis point gain from 58.3% in 2022, our finest since post-crisis times. Q4 2023 hit 55.8%, under our under-57% target and better than the KBW large-cap peer average of 58.1%. This came from 12% revenue growth to $28.4 billion outpacing 4.2% expense rise to $15.9 billion, with NIM at 3.68%—up 22 basis points year-over-year—and 9% non-interest income growth from capital markets and treasury volumes, similar to JPMorgan in rate-hike periods.

Key drivers included expense control: flat compensation via 2.1% headcount reduction to 48,000 through attrition and targeted hires, plus $250 million procurement savings from supplier consolidation like Bank of America's efforts. Occupancy costs dropped 5% with hybrid work, saving $40 million yearly.

Tech played a big role: Temenos Transact migration automated 45% of loan originations, cutting times to under 24 hours and costs 18%. Feedzai AI fraud detection prevented $1.2 billion losses—30% better—and UiPath RPA saved $120 million annually. This aligns with Wells Fargo and Citigroup upgrades, aiming for AWS cloud-native by 2025-end.

Regionally, U.S. (65% revenues) reached 54.1% efficiency from Southeast deposit growth to $180 billion and Pinnacle Private Client cross-sell. Europe (20%) improved to 59.4% from 62.1% via Irish mortgage exit and ESG lending in Dublin, despite Basel IV and ECB caps compressing NIM to 2.95%. Asia-Pacific (15%) hit 57.2% with 22% AUM growth in Singapore/Hong Kong, aided by Mumbai tech center for India's payments.

For 2024, we target under 55%, stretching to 53%, via 10-12% revenue growth (NIM 3.75-3.85%, 8% fees from ISO 20022), $300 million gen-AI savings with Palantir, and 6% revenue tech/risk spend at $1.7 billion, backing CET1 of 11.8% and 15% ROE above 13% peer median.

Turning to reserves, we had a $175 million release in Q3 under CECL, versus $250 million build prior quarter and $300 million last year, aiding earnings. This reflected better portfolio performance, easing macro, and model tweaks projecting lifetime ECL on our $650 billion loans.

Macro de-escalation: U.S. unemployment to 4.1%, GDP 2.8%, inflation 2.4%; global ECB cuts/China stimulus trimmed recession odds to 25%. Portfolio wins: consumer delinquencies to 2.1% (credit cards/auto strong), C&I charge-offs to 45 bps; NCOs $220 million or 32 bps under 45 bps average/peers. Model refresh with Palantir GenAI boosted PD accuracy 12%, releasing $80 million overlays; $50 million energy recoveries.

By region: U.S. (72% loans) $140 million release, CRE office NPLs 1.2% at 65% LTV; Europe (15%) $25 million on corporates/UK mortgages; APAC (8%) $15 million on ASEAN SMEs with Sea Limited; other flat.

Coverage is robust: ALLL 1.92% of loans (vs. 1.95% Q2, 2.10% prior year, peer 1.75%); 285% of NPLs ($12.5B ALLL / $4.4B NPLs vs. JPM 260%); 115% criticized (peer 105%). Unallocated $1.8B (14%). De-risked $5B non-core CRE, office to 8%; Risk 3.0 cuts delinquencies 25%. Q4 provisions $100-200M; downside covers 2.5x losses. CRE watch: $2.5B monitored, book 22% CRE vs. peers 28%.

For outlook on loans and credit, we guide 5-7% full-year 2024 growth adjusted. C&I (45%) 6-8% on manufacturing/energy, $1.2B renewables with NextEra, middle-market utilization 52%, digital portal. CRE (25%) 2-4%, office 8% at 1.8x DSCR; multifamily/industrial strong, Sun Belt 7%+ pipeline, de-risking Midwest. Consumer (20%) 4-6%, auto 9% at 740 FICO, mortgages 3% at 6.5% rates, 35% digital jumbos.

Tech support: SymphonyAI GenAI 15% accuracy boost, SOFR swaps at LIBOR+125bps edge, equipment leasing 15%. NCOs 25-35 bps (Q1 28bps), delinquencies 62bps under 85bps average/peers. Consumer 1.2%/0.4%, C&I 0.3%, CRE 0.5%; ACL 1.25% ($2.8B), 280% NCOs. Southwest best, California monitored. ML vintage analysis 92% precision, DTI to 42%; syndications 20%. ROCE to 11%+ 2025 on 75bps cuts.

We continue to maintain a strong capital position with a CET1 ratio of 12.8%. We are pleased with the progress we are making on our strategic initiatives, and we remain confident in our ability to deliver sustainable value for our shareholders.

With the Fed terminal around 4.75-5%, full-year EPS $7.80-$8.00 (12-15% growth), NIM 3.70%. $250B liquidity, LCR 125%.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, that is 1 then the star key. Our first question comes from Mike Sullivan with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Sullivan:
Good morning. Can you provide some color on the drivers behind your NIM expansion and non-interest revenue surge this quarter?

David Marshall:
Good morning, Mike. Absolutely, our NIM expansion to 3.72% was propelled by a low deposit beta of 32%, strategic asset repricing in commercial loans, and steady loan growth across high-yield segments. On non-interest, the 22% jump to $5.1 billion came from wealth management net new assets, investment banking mandates including that rail carve-out and IPO rebound, plus fixed income trading gains—our diversification is really shining through.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jennifer Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Lee:
Good morning. What is your outlook for efficiency ratio progression and loan growth into the second half?

Robert Kline:
Good morning, Jennifer. We're on track for under 55% efficiency in 2024 through revenue leverage, gen-AI cost savings, and disciplined tech investments. Loan growth stays at 5-7%, with C&I leading on capex and renewables, tempered CRE growth focused on industrial/multifamily, and steady consumer—our digital and specialty finance initiatives provide tailwinds.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of commercial real estate trends on your loan portfolio and reserve coverage?

Elena Vasquez:
Good morning, Tom. CRE is 22-25% of our book, with office tightly managed at 8% and strong 1.8x DSCR or 65% LTV underwriting. Delinquencies are low at 0.5-1.2%, and we've de-risked via $5 billion sales and restructurings. Coverage is peer-leading at 1.92% ALLL to loans, 285% to NPLs, providing 2.5x buffer in stress—our AI risk tools and diversification keep quality pristine.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to David Marshall for any closing remarks.

David Marshall:
Thank you for your interest in Apex Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
